run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T18:38:09Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained at the signal level: the frontend-proxy trace metric carries a small number of STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans on the operation `ingress`, and the 5-minute error rate of those spans repeatedly reads exactly 0.011111111111111112 per second, matching the alert annotation value 0.01111111111111111. Over 17:38:09-18:55:36Z there were 15.21 error ingress spans against 27,090 non-error ingress spans (about 0.06%). The proxy's own access log records every one of those failures as `503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}` against upstream host 100.70.32.128:8080, cluster `frontend` - i.e. the frontend service (ClusterIP 100.70.32.128, single endpoint pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-ssc7t at 100.96.4.88) terminated the connection before response headers were sent. The paired `router frontend egress` span records error=true with http.status_code=0, and the calling load-generator GET span records 503. The frontend workload itself shows no crash: 1/1 ready, one pod, restartCount 0, no last termination state, zero STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans in every interval checked, and all nodes Ready with no pressure. Two candidate mechanisms remain unresolved rather than proven: the frontend container runs at a cpu limit of 100m and had about 32% of CFS periods throttled (frontend-proxy 30m, about 6.6%), which can stall request handling; and a keep-alive reuse race between the Envoy upstream pool and the frontend HTTP server would produce the same fast UC resets. Throttling did not co-vary with the error bursts (flat 30.6-35.4% while 5-minute error counts swung between 0 and 3.33), and the frontend container produced no log lines at all in the window, so the frontend-side reason for the connection terminations is not established. Separately, fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-xdwst was OOMKilled (exit 137) at 18:38:11Z and restarted once; this coincides with the alert start but is not tied to the frontend-proxy 503s (which begin at 18:13:26Z and hit frontend routes) and is reported as a separate condition of another workload. No pre-incident baseline is available, so an increase in error rate could not be verified.

claims.text: The alert's data source is traces_span_metrics_calls_total for service_name="frontend-proxy": only the operation `ingress` carries errors. For 17:38:09-18:55:36Z, the increase over 4647s was 15.211 STATUS_CODE_ERROR ingress spans versus 27090.254 STATUS_CODE_UNSET ingress spans (and 27103.437 UNSET spans on `router frontend egress`). Span counts are not request counts.

The 5-minute rate of frontend-proxy `ingress` STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans oscillated between 0 and 0.0185 spans/s from 18:14:09 to 18:55:36Z and repeatedly returned exactly 0.011111111111111112, matching the alert annotation value 0.01111111111111111; corresponding 5-minute error-span counts were 0, 1.11, 3.33, 3.33, 3.25 and 1.24.

In the sampled error traces, frontend-proxy `ingress` spans carry status tags error=true, http.status_code="503", otel.status_code="ERROR", and their child `router frontend egress` spans carry error="true", http.status_code="0"; the calling load-generator `GET` spans record http.status_code="503". Trace 006109e39dbc3e0e38ea35e8110e2b5c contains exactly four spans: load-generator user_browse_product -> GET(503) -> frontend-proxy ingress(503) -> frontend-proxy router frontend egress(error, status 0).

frontend-proxy access logs record the failures exactly as `"GET /api/products/... HTTP/1.1" 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} - "-" 0 95 <8-1175> - ... "100.70.32.128:8080" frontend ...` - Envoy response flag UC with code detail upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}, upstream host 100.70.32.128:8080, upstream cluster `frontend`, no upstream service time, durations 8-1175 ms. Observed timestamps: 18:13:26, 18:20:14, 18:21:10, 18:21:53, 18:28:02, 18:31:30 (x2), 18:32:18, 18:36:46, 18:36:57, 18:37:30, 18:37:58, 18:39:26, 18:48:03 UTC on 2026-11-16.

100.70.32.128 is the ClusterIP of Service `frontend` in namespace otel-demo (port 8080, selector opentelemetry.io/name=frontend); that Service has a single endpoint, pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-ssc7t with podIP 100.96.4.88 on node i-029c97e90b3730286. The proxy is pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-bf4lq, podIP 100.96.4.190, matching the downstream local address in the 503 log lines.

The frontend workload shows no failure in its own signals: Deployment frontend reports replicas 1, ready 1, available 1, with Available and Progressing True; its only pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-ssc7t is Running and ready with restartCount 0 and no last termination state; and the frontend trace metric records STATUS_CODE_ERROR = 0 in every 17-minute bucket queried from 18:15 to 18:55Z, while non-error frontend spans run at roughly 43,000-52,000 per 17 minutes.

All 22 otel-demo pods were created between 17:59:11Z and 18:01:18Z (frontend at 17:59:11Z, frontend-proxy at 17:59:13Z), and every Deployment in the namespace is at its desired replica count (fraud-detection 2/2, all others 1/1). The only pod restart visible in the window's events is fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-xdwst (Pulled/Created/Started container at 18:38:11Z); no event mentions frontend or frontend-proxy.

Resource configuration and CPU throttling: the frontend container has limits cpu=100m/memory=200Mi (requests 50m/100Mi) and had 32.2% of its CFS periods throttled over the window (pod-level 32.9%), holding at 30.6-35.4% in each 5-minute slice; the frontend-proxy container has limits cpu=30m/memory=50Mi and had 6.6% throttled (1.1-7.7% per 5-minute slice). Peak working set was 122.8Mi for the frontend container (of 200Mi) and 19.7Mi for frontend-proxy (of 50Mi). Neither container has a readiness or liveness probe configured.

All five cluster nodes report Ready=True with MemoryPressure=False, DiskPressure=False, PIDPressure=False and 4 allocatable CPUs, including i-029c97e90b3730286 which hosts both the frontend and frontend-proxy pods.

Separate finding on another workload: pod fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-xdwst (container fraud-detection) shows lastState terminated with reason OOMKilled, exitCode 137, finishedAt 2026-11-16T18:38:11Z and restartCount 1; the fraud-detection Deployment sets memory limit 400Mi (request 200Mi), and that pod's container working set peaked at 376.3Mi within a 399.89Mi pod total.

Error spans elsewhere in the namespace during the same window are not frontend-proxy errors: the only nonzero ERROR series besides frontend-proxy `ingress` are flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream on ad, fraud-detection and recommendation (about 1-4 spans per 17 minutes each), while frontend, checkout and payment show 0 ERROR spans at every point. fraud-detection's ERROR spans are limited to that flagd EventStream operation; its `orders process` and `orders receive` spans carry no status.

The frontend-proxy error series has no samples earlier than this incident window: the earliest timestamps returned for service_name="frontend-proxy" begin at 18:14:09Z, and every workload pod in otel-demo was created no earlier than 17:59:11Z, so no pre-incident behaviour of this series exists to compare against.

Candidate mechanism 1: the frontend container's cpu limit of 100m (32% CFS throttling) starves its request handling, so in-flight connections are aborted before response headers and Envoy reports UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}. This is plausible but unproven and not correlated in time: throttling stayed at 30.6-35.4% in every 5-minute slice while 5-minute error counts varied between 0 and 3.33.

Candidate mechanism 2: the resets are a keep-alive connection reuse race between the frontend-proxy Envoy upstream pool and the frontend HTTP server, which would close an already-reused connection before any response. This is consistent with several failing requests completing in only 8-23 ms with no upstream service time recorded, but no Envoy cluster/keep-alive configuration or frontend HTTP timeout values were available to confirm it.

Counter-evidence against treating the frontend as broadly broken: frontend itself recorded 0 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans throughout the window, its pod has restartCount 0 with no last termination, the Deployment is 1/1 ready, all nodes are Ready with no pressure, and the frontend-proxy error volume is small - 15.21 error ingress spans against 27,090 non-error ingress spans (about 0.06%) across 4647 s, with 5-minute error counts between 0 and 3.33.

Rejected: the fraud-detection OOMKill/restart at 18:38:11Z caused this alert. The frontend-proxy 503 UC log lines begin at 18:13:26Z, well before that restart, and affect frontend routes (/, /api/products/*, /api/data*, /api/recommendations) rather than checkout or fraud-detection; fraud-detection's own ERROR spans are only flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream and are not frontend-proxy errors.

Rejected: a frontend pod crash, eviction or rollout produced the 503s. Pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-ssc7t is Running and ready with restartCount 0 and no last termination state, the frontend Deployment is 1/1 ready, and the window's Kubernetes events contain no entry for the frontend pod.

Obtain the frontend's application output for the 14 timestamped 503 windows (18:13-18:48Z) and inspect it for handler panics, request timeouts or idle-connection closes, and review the Envoy cluster/route configuration (upstream keep-alive, idle timeout, retry policy) against the frontend HTTP server's keep-alive settings; one of these is needed to choose between the two remaining mechanisms.

Review the frontend container cpu limit (100m) and request (50m) given the measured 32% CFS throttling, and the fraud-detection memory limit (400Mi) against a 399.89Mi peak working set that produced the OOMKill; the latter is a separate problem from this alert.

gaps: The frontend container produced no stdout/stderr lines in 17:38:09-18:55:36Z (four fetch_pod_logs calls returned status no_data with 0 bytes read), so the frontend-side reason it terminated connections (handler panic, timeout, keep-alive close, etc.) could not be read; these no_data views show only that nothing was returned, not that nothing happened.

No pre-incident baseline: the query for the frontend-proxy error series over 16:38:09-17:38:09Z returned status no_data (unknown, not zero), the series' earliest samples in this Run begin at 18:14:09Z, and all pods were created 17:59-18:01Z, so an error-rate increase versus normal operation is unverified.

The alert rule itself could not be inspected: list_prometheus_rules returned no rules for rule_name=RequestErrorRate and no rules at all for type=alert (both status no_data), so the alert expression, threshold and for-duration are unverified; the 0.011111111 value matches the 5-minute error-span rate only by value.

No Envoy/application configuration (upstream keep-alive, idle and request timeouts, retry policy) or network-layer drop/retransmit telemetry was available, so the mechanism behind the upstream connection terminations is unresolved.

The conventional HTTP server metric http_server_request_duration_seconds_count does not exist in this Run's Prometheus (get_series and get_all_labels returned no_data), so proxy error rate could only be measured through traces_span_metrics_calls_total, which counts spans rather than requests.
Traces are a sampled view (8 traces / 74 spans in the error-tag search), so no complete call chain or exact failure rate can be derived from them; spans from services not returned remain unknown.

Whether the frontend is functionally impaired is not established: its own error, restart and readiness signals show no failure, and the only evidence of trouble at the frontend is the proxy-side Envoy diagnostic.
Change history is not integrated in this Run (listed under not_integrated), so a recent configuration change to the frontend, frontend-proxy or their resource limits cannot be checked.
next_steps: Read frontend application logs for 18:13-18:48Z once stdout is available for the frontend container, capturing panics, timeouts or connection-close messages.
Compare the frontend-proxy Envoy cluster configuration (upstream keep-alive/idle timeouts, retry policy, max requests per connection) with the frontend HTTP server keep-alive settings.
Evaluate raising the frontend cpu limit/request above 100m/50m given 32% CFS throttling, and add the readiness/liveness probes that are currently absent on both frontend and frontend-proxy.
Treat the fraud-detection OOMKill (400Mi limit vs 399.89Mi peak) as its own issue: review its memory limit and heap/GC behaviour.
Re-check the frontend-proxy error rate once a longer baseline exists, and verify the RequestErrorRate rule definition in the Alertmanager/Prometheus that owns it.
